Incident Type: FIXED
Material: GROUND WATER, AND MACHINE COOLANT MIXTURE

Suspected Responsible Party: BOEING

Medium Affected: OTHER
Suspected Responsible Party:
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 41.852598, -72.643702 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)
Reported Spill Volume: 79 gallon
Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS A SPILL OF 300 L OF DIESEL FROM A 352 EXCAVATOR DUE TO A MECHANICAL FAILURE (FROZEN LINE). AT THE TIME, THEY WERE TRYING TO REMOVE AN OLD, ABANDONED BOX CULVERT WHICH WAS UNDER THE ROAD WHEN THE SPILL OCCURRED. THE SPILL LANDED ON A HEAVILY COMPACTED FROZEN CLAY BASE. NO STORM SEWERS, CATCH BASINS OR WATERWAYS WERE IMPACTED. PADS AND BOOMS WERE PLACED AROUND THE GROUND AND GRANULAR ABSORBENT. THE AREA WAS BERMED AS WELL TO PREVENT THE DIESEL FROM MIGRATING. THE CONTAMINATED SOIL IS CURRENTLY BEING REMOVED BY AN EXCAVATOR. THE MATERIAL WILL THEN BE TRANSFERRED INTO A LINED DISPOSAL BIN. CALLER INDICATES THAT HE IS WATCHING THE DIESEL AND IT HAS NOT IMPACTED THE DETROIT RIVER WHICH IS 50 METRES AWAY. THE EXCAVATOR IS BEING REPAIRED AND SOIL SAMPLES WILL BE TAKEN. CALLER ANTICIPATES THE CLEANUP TO BE FINISHED IN AN HOUR AND WILL UPDATE SAC WHEN THIS OCCURS.

Report Description///POTENTIAL RELEASE REPORT/// ///CRITICAL INCIDENT COMMUNICATIONS (CIC) REPORT - INITIAL - F/V ARCTIC SEA - AGROUND VESSEL WITH 9 POB IVO ST. GEORGE ISLAND, AK - 05 JAN 2026/// INITIAL INCIDENT TYPE: MASS RESCUE OPERATION LOCATION: ST. GEORGE ISLAND, ALASKA TIME INCIDENT OCCURRED: 0812 EST / 1312Z, 05JAN2026 TIME OF INITIAL REPORT TO NCC: 1350 EST / 1850Z, 05JAN2026 NAME OF REPORTING UNIT: USCG ARCTIC DISTRICT INITIAL: • ON JANUARY 5TH, FISHING VESSEL (F/V) ARCTIC SEA WAS DISABLED AND RAN AGROUND ON THE NORTH SIDE OF ST. GEORGE ISLAND, ALASKA. • HER SISTER SHIP, F/V NORTH SEA WAS ABLE TO BROADCAST THE INFORMATION TO USCG ARCTIC DISTRICT. • AFTER THE F/V ARCTIC SEA RAN AGROUND, THE VESSEL BEGAN TAKING ON WATER. • DUE TO RUNNING AGROUND, THE FLOODING OF THE VESSEL HAS STOPPED AND HAS NOT PROGRESSED ABOVE THE WATERLINE. • THERE ARE NINE CREWMEMBERS ONBOARD, AND THEY HAVE ALL DONNED SURVIVAL SUITS, INFLATED THEIR LIFE RAFT, AND ACTIVATED THEIR EPIRB. • THE CREW MEMBERS HAVE NOT ABANDONED SHIP AND BELIEVE THEY ARE IN NO DANGER OF CAPSIZING. • A COAST GUARD HELICOPTER FROM USCG AIR STATION KODIAK (CG-6035) IS ENROUTE TO THE F/V ARCTIC SEA WITH AN ANTICIPATED ARRIVAL TIME OF 1450 EST / 1950Z. • A COAST GUARD C-130 IS ON SCENE AND MAINTAINING RADIO COMMUNICATION WITH THE F/V ARCTIC SEA EVERY 30 MINUTES. • CG-6035 INTENDS TO HOIST ALL NINE CREWMEMBERS WITHIN THE SAME SORTIE AND TRANSPORT THEM TO ST. PAUL MEDICAL CENTER. • ON SCENE WEATHER HAS THE WINDS COMING OUT OF THE NORTH-NORTHWEST AT 25 KNOTS, SEAS ARE FOUR FEET, WITH HALF A MILE OF VISIBILITY. • THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN WITH CONCURRENCE FROM BOTH AREAS. • NCC WILL PROVIDE AN EMAIL UPDATE ONCE ALL NINE CREWMEMBERS ARE HOISTED AND SAFELY ABOARD CG-6035.

Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** ON APRIL 4TH, 2013 AT APPROXIMATELY 11:16 AM KOCH PIPELINE RECEIVED ADDITIONAL INFORMATION FROM AN ORIGINAL RELEASE AND SUBSEQUENT REPAIR AT A PUMP STATION LOCATED AT 9145 FM 563 IN LIBERTY, TEXAS. THE ORIGINAL RELEASE THAT OCCURRED ON MARCH 29TH, 2013 AT APPROX 3:30 PM. WAS BELIEVED TO BE LESS THAN 5 GALLONS FROM THE AFFECTED PIPING AT THE LOCATION. THE SITE WAS BLOCKED IN FOR REPAIR AND REPAIRS WERE MADE TO THE STATION ON MONDAY 4-1-2013. DURING THE COURSE OF THE INVESTIGATION IT WAS FOUND THAT A LOSS IN PRESSURE AFFECTED MORE PIPING THAN WAS ORIGINALLY BELIEVED. AFTER RECEIVING THIS INFORMATION CALCULATIONS WERE PERFORMED ON APRIL 4TH AT 11:00 AND THE ESTIMATED RELEASE TO ATMOSPHERE WAS ESTIMATED TO BE 65.3 GALLONS.

Report Description- USCG SECTOR KEY WEST REPORTED AN 85 FOOT VESSEL ANCHORED NORTH OF KEY WEST, LISTING TO ONE SIDE. THE VESSEL CAUGHT ON FIRE, FULLY ENGULFED DOWN TO THE WATERLINE, AND IS STILL FLOATING. - THE ANCHOR IS STILL HOLDING, AND THE OWNER WILL GO OUT BEFORE SUNSET TO ADD A SECOND ANCHOR AND LIGHT TO MARK IT. - TWO PERSONS ONBOARD WERE DISEMBARKED OFF THE BOW BY USCG STATION KEY WEST 45" RESPONSE BOAT. POLLUTION POTENTIAL: 75 GALLONS OF DIESEL AND A FEW GALLONS OF FUEL ONBOARD. - ADDITIONAL VESSEL INFORMATION: 100 TO 114 GROSS TONS (BREADTH: 25 FEET, DEPTH: 8 FEET). - NO ADDITIONAL CONTACT INFORMATION WAS PROVIDED. - THERE IS CURRENTLY NO MEDIA ATTENTION, BUT PA WAS NOTIFIED AND A TWITTER POST WAS MADE WITH A PHOTO OF THE VESSEL.

IN SUPPORT OF THE BP MC252 RESPONSE: OFFLOADING RECOVERED PRODUCT FROM THE MSRC OSRB 402 TO THE CENAC BARGE, A KINK DEVELOPED IN THE HOSE. PUMPING OPERATIONS WERE SHUT DOWN. THIS WAS LOCATED AT BENNETS CORNERS ROAD IN MEMPHIS, NY. THE CREW STATED THE CAR MAY HAVE COLLIDED INTO THE CROSSING GATES. NO VEHICLE OCCUPANTS WERE SEEN NEARBY. ONONDAGA COUNTY OFFICE OF EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT WAS NOTIFIED AND RESPONDING. AMTRAK PASSENGER OPERATIONS WAS CONTACTED AND STATED THIS IS AN AMTRAK LINE BUT NO DELAYS ARE EXPECTED. ONONDAGA COUNTY WAS UPDATED AND REPORTED THE VEHICLE IS UNOCCUPIED AND THE DRIVER CANNOT BE LOCATED. THE NF TRAIN DISPATCHER WAS UPDATED. THE CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS MANAGER WAS NOTIFIED.

STARTING AT APPROXIMATELY 0600 HOURS, FLOOD WATERS ROSE ONTO THE SERVICE CENTER PROPERTY. BY 0800 HOURS, THERE WAS APPROXIMATELY FOUR FEET OF WATER OVER OUR PROPERTY AND INTO OUR SERVICE BUILDING. AT THIS TIME, WHILE ASSESSING DAMAGE TO THE PROPERTY, A HEAVY SHEEN OF OIL (MOST LIKELY AUTOMOTIVE TYPE OILS) WAS OBSERVED INSIDE OF THE BUILDING ON THE REMAINING WATER. SUNPRO, A LOCAL SPILL CLEANUP CONTRACTOR, HAS BEEN CALLED IN TO CONTAIN AND CLEANUP THE RELEASED MATERIALS. THE MATERIALS WERE ORIGINALLY STORED ON SHELVING IN A LOW LYING WORK/TOOL STORAGE AREA.

Skytruth Analysis

Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK (ALONG THE REVETMENT) ON AUGUST 10, 2011, SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708)
